disposition_mapping.rationale: The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) rejected maximalist's merger of calendar/assumption issuance with top-down target-setting: the downside scenario is an estimate requiring an accountable human author (KB-04), and automated macro/FX feeds are unreliable for frontier/thin markets, so a human must substantively calibrate, not merely approve, the draft. T-01 keeps the FP&A manager as issuer of record, adds versioning (finance_domain) and multi-channel/offline distribution (emerging_economy) as survivability conditions, while permitting agentic drafting assistance (agentic_architect).

Although unconstrained by design, the council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) held against maximalist's absorption of this step into kickoff with CEO/CFO reduced to ratify/override: a machine-generated default that a human merely overrides quietly shifts accountability from the executive to the model. T-02 keeps top-down target-setting as a discrete CEO/CFO decision, adds decision-support tooling (agentic_architect) and a recalibration touchpoint against first-pass bottom-up data (finance_domain) to address the real driver of challenge-round volume, without eliminating the deliberate human decision.

The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, emerging_economy) converged against maximalist's merger of revenue/volume planning into a single orchestrated bottom-up pass: distinct ownership lines must map to distinct, traceable steps so a variance six months later resolves to a named BU head, not a blended planning engine. The step is retained as BU-head-owned with analytics-assisted drafting only, plus an offline-capable submission channel (emerging_economy).

Same reasoning as ABB-03: cost-centre owners work off different source data and carry different accountability than BU heads, so the council majority rejected merging this into a combined agentic pass. Retained as a distinct, owner-accountable step with drafting assistance, a manual HRIS/headcount override path (emerging_economy), and an offline submission channel.

Capex retains its own governance rhythm (multi-year phasing, depreciation handoff, threshold-triggered business case) that the council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, emerging_economy, agentic_architect) agreed must not be folded into general cost or revenue planning. The business case above threshold remains a literal, mandatory input (ABB-R-04); a deterministic intake-validation function may check completeness but cannot waive or auto-approve it, and the depreciation schedule is surfaced explicitly as finance_domain required.

This is the strongest automation candidate across the council (maximalist, agentic_architect, hitl_designer, finance_domain, emerging_economy all converge on system-assisted consolidation), but the majority rejects maximalist's framing of full automation with FP&A reduced to passive exception-handling. T-06 keeps accounting policies and central FX assumptions as literal, fixed-configuration inputs (ABB-R-05, ABB-R-07; KB-06, KB-07, KB-08), adds explicit intercompany identification-and-elimination sub-checks (finance_domain, accounting_standards, agentic_architect, pragmatist) because the step's own basis-equivalence claim to actuals pulls IFRS 10 logic into scope, specifies halt-and-escalate rather than silent-plug failure behaviour (agentic_architect), and retains a mandatory FP&A-analyst reconciliation checkpoint plus a degraded-mode ingestion path for low-connectivity units (emerging_economy).

Maximalist's proposal to dissolve review-and-challenge into a continuous, always-on anomaly-flagging function with no discrete step was held against by six of seven council members (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, emerging_economy, accounting_standards noting the architectural fork): challenge is an adversarial negotiation, not a data-freshness property, and a flag system that silently auto-passes material items is a rubber stamp. T-07 is retained as a distinct step, restructured to combine exception-triage (hitl_designer) with capped, dated iteration rounds and escalation (pragmatist, emerging_economy), mandatory documented human resolution on flagged items, and a store-and-forward channel for submitters without live tooling (emerging_economy).

Unanimous across the council: board approval is a governance act, not a computation, and must remain a human, accountable act with no agentic decision authority, strictly before lock (ABB-R-08, ABB-R-11). The only enrichment, per hitl_designer, is that board materials must substantively show assumptions, downside-scenario impact and unresolved challenge items rather than a bare top-line number, with pack adequacy remaining an accountable FP&A responsibility rather than an unreviewed automated export (addressing hitl_designer's conflict with agentic_architect on this point).

The mechanical load/lock action can be agent-executed (maximalist, agentic_architect), but the council majority (hitl_designer, finance_domain, accounting_standards, emerging_economy) requires that lock not take effect until a named individual distinct from whoever last touched consolidation independently confirms the loaded version reconciles to the board-approved artifact -- correctness-at-lock is prioritised over speed-to-lock, resolving the finance_domain/agentic_architect conflict in favour of confirmed correctness. The locked version is also exported to a durable, vendor-independent format (emerging_economy) so access to the budget of record does not depend on a single vendor's licensing, and strict ordering after board approval (ABB-R-08) is preserved by making board approval the sole trigger.

steps.description: An Assumptions Agent drafts central planning assumptions (inflation, FX, interest rates) and a parameterised downside macro scenario from licensed market-data feeds and scenario templates. The FP&A manager reviews, substantively adjusts where local market conditions diverge from feed coverage (not a light edit-and-approve pass), and is the accountable issuer of record. Every issuance and any mid-cycle revision carries a version stamp so submitters can never work off superseded assumptions. Distribution is multi-channel (document plus portal), not portal-only, so units without reliable always-on connectivity still receive the calendar and assumptions on time.
steps.name: Issue calendar and central planning assumptions (model-assisted, human-issued)

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets against the strategic plan and the issued central assumptions, optionally stress-testing candidate targets against the downside scenario using a decision-support tool. The tool computes; it does not decide, and no agent sets or defaults a target on the executives' behalf. A recalibration touchpoint is scheduled once first-pass bottom-up submissions land, so unachievable targets are surfaced before full consolidation rather than discovered only in review and challenge.
steps.name: Set and calibrate top-down targets

steps.description: Business unit heads remain the named, accountable authors of revenue and volume plans. A drafting copilot may pre-populate templates from prior actuals and the central assumptions, but it is advisory only and never submits on the BU head's behalf. A lightweight, offline-capable submission path (templated spreadsheet, batch upload) is maintained as a first-class channel alongside any live planning tool, so units with limited connectivity are not structurally excluded.
steps.name: Revenue and volume plans (owner-accountable, analytics-supported)

steps.description: Cost centre owners remain the named, accountable authors of cost centre and headcount budgets, kept distinct from revenue/volume ownership because the drivers, source data (HRIS, open positions, attrition) and accountability chain differ. Drafting assistance is permitted; authorship and sign-off are not transferable to a model. A manual override/correction path is retained at the cost-centre-owner level where HRIS/payroll data does not fully integrate with planning tools, and an offline-capable submission channel is maintained.
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets (owner-accountable, analytics-supported)

steps.description: Business unit heads author capex requests and, above threshold, a written business case that a human writes and a human reads. A deterministic Intake Validation function checks completeness against a fixed checklist and routes incomplete submissions back with a specific deficiency list; it can never waive the business-case requirement or auto-approve a request. Capex requests carry forward the resulting depreciation schedule as an explicit output, since that schedule is a direct input to the P&L and cash-flow legs of consolidation.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests with threshold-triggered business case (intake-validated)

steps.description: A Consolidation Agent aggregates revenue/volume, cost/headcount and capex submissions into a draft three-statement budget, applying the accounting policies used for actuals and the central FX assumptions as fixed configuration (never agent-inferred), and performs explicit sub-checks: balance-sheet balance, cash-flow derivation from P&L/BS movements, and intercompany identification-and-elimination (made explicit because the step's own basis-equivalence claim to actuals pulls IFRS 10 elimination discipline into scope). On any reconciliation break, stale-feed condition, or unmatched intercompany balance, the agent halts and escalates to the FP&A analyst with a diff report rather than forcing a balance; it never silently plugs. Every run is logged with input snapshot, policy/FX version, and output. A degraded-mode ingestion path (batch/offline submission) is supported for units without integrated ERP/EPM connectivity, so straight-through automation does not implicitly exclude them.
steps.name: Consolidation engine with mandatory exception review and intercompany elimination

steps.description: The draft budget is re-derived automatically on each revised submission, and an exception-flagging function highlights material variances against targets, prior iterations and benchmarks so the FP&A manager and CFO focus attention on what matters rather than re-deriving statements by hand. Flagged items require a real, documented conversation with the submitter and a recorded resolution; nothing material is waved through as 'reviewed, no action.' Iteration is bounded by a capped number of rounds with a dated escalation path to CFO/CEO if a submitter has not converged by the final round. A store-and-forward (asynchronous) iteration channel is retained for submitters without live collaborative-tooling access.
steps.name: Exception-triaged review and challenge
outputs: Documented resolution log for flagged items

steps.description: The board approves the budget, but is given substantive information to interrogate, not a top-line number alone: the central assumptions, the downside scenario and its quantified impact, and a summary of what was challenged and left unresolved in review. Board materials are machine-assembled from the current draft but their adequacy is the accountable responsibility of the FP&A manager preparing the pack, not an unreviewed automated export. This step remains entirely free of agentic decision authority.
inputs: Documented resolution log for flagged items
steps.name: Board approval (substantive, assumption-visible)

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (independent confirmer, distinct from consolidation preparer)
steps.description: A Load-and-Lock Agent loads the board-approved figures into the planning/EPM system and sets the version to locked, triggered only by receipt of the board-approved artifact (no calendar date, no confidence-score trigger) with hash-checked pre-load validation against the board document. Before the lock takes effect, a named accountable individual distinct from whoever last touched the consolidation run independently confirms the loaded version reconciles exactly to the board-approved output. The locked version is exported to a durable, vendor-independent format so a lapsed licence or outage cannot sever access to the budget of record. Any post-lock change requires a documented, sign-off change-control reopening, never a silent edit.
steps.name: Load and lock approved version (agent-executed, independently confirmed)
